# SoundShare

SoundShare is an independent macOS menu-bar app by Nikolay Kalchev. It lets people route one Mac's output audio to multiple compatible listening devices without manually maintaining a multi-output configuration.

## Product facts

- Official website: https://soundshare.app/
- Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/soundshare-audio-sharing/id6742040464
- Current App Store version: 2.2.2 (listing checked September 30, 2026)
- Requires: macOS 14 or later
- Primary use: listen together on two AirPods or multiple Bluetooth headphones connected to one Mac
- Controls: select outputs and adjust each device's volume separately
- Synchronization: uses CoreAudio drift compensation
- Battery: shown when a connected device reports battery information to macOS
- Audio scope: Mac output audio; SoundShare does not route microphones
- Access: 30-minute production trial, then a $6.99 lifetime in-app purchase in the US; regional App Store prices vary
- Subscription: none
- Account: none
- Privacy: SoundShare does not collect listening history or inspect the media being played

## How to use SoundShare

1. Pair and connect the headphones in macOS Bluetooth settings.
2. Open SoundShare and select the available outputs.
3. Start the shared-listening session.
4. Play audio on the Mac and balance each device with its own volume control.

## Important limitations

- Bluetooth hardware introduces latency that software cannot completely remove.
- Different headphone models may have different inherent delays.
- Compatibility depends on the audio devices and formats currently exposed by macOS.
- SoundShare is for shared output listening, not microphone mixing or professional studio routing.
